posts.summary: The bill would direct the Bureau of Land Management to sell the federal government's reversionary interest in approximately 8.43 acres of land in Sacramento, California, to the current landowner. posts.title: A bill to provide for the equitable settlement of certain Indian land disputes regarding land in Illinois, and for other purposes.
posts.label: 📌 Presented to President
posts.summary: The bill would give the U.S. Court of Federal Claims the authority to hear a land dispute claim by the Miami Tribe of Oklahoma based on an old treaty, requiring the court to decide the case without applying statutes of limitations or delay-based defenses, but only if the tribe files within one year. posts.title: Protect College Sports Act of 2026

posts.summary: The bill would establish a geothermal ombudsman within the Interior Department's Bureau of Land Management to streamline the permitting process for geothermal energy projects on federal lands. posts.summary: The bill would require the Department of the Interior to grant a right-of-way through the Blue Ridge Parkway to create an emergency exit route from Wintergreen, Virginia, but only after the agency completes several studies. These include evaluating alternative exit routes that don't cross federal land, analyzing how fire behavior might affect the area, and conducting required environmental and historic preservation reviews.

If the county stops using the land for that purpose, ownership would revert back to the federal government, and the county would bear all costs associated with the transfer, including surveys and environmental assessments.

posts.note: Energy and Natural Resources, without amendment, without written report

posts.summary: The bill would allow the Department of Energy to transfer a uranium milling site near Moab, Utah, to Grand County at no cost once cleanup of radioactive waste is complete. The transfer would include restrictions preventing the county from later selling or giving any part of the land to private parties or nonprofits, and the Department of Energy would retain rights to water and well access needed for ongoing groundwater cleanup.

posts.title: National Prescribed Fire Act of 2025
posts.label: 📋 Reported by committee
posts.note: Energy and Natural Resources, with an amendment in the nature of a substitute, without written report
posts.summary: The bill would direct the federal government to significantly increase the use of controlled fires on public lands managed by the Interior Department and Forest Service, particularly in western and southeastern national forests. Over ten years, it would require these agencies to expand prescribed fire operations annually and establish a financial assistance program to help states, tribes, and other partners conduct these fires in priority areas. The measure also aims to support Indigenous cultural burning practices, expand employment and training for prescribed fire workers, and coordinate with the EPA and state agencies to monitor air quality impacts from the increased burning.

posts.summary: The bill would authorize a land exchange in Alaska between the Chugach Alaska Corporation, an Alaska Native regional corporation, and the federal government. If Chugach transfers approximately 231,000 acres of subsurface rights to the Department of the Interior within a year, the federal government would transfer approximately 65,374 acres of land in the Chugach region (on the Kenai Peninsula and near Prince William Sound) to Chugach in return, with certain village corporation lands and shareholder homesites excluded from the exchange.

posts.note: Energy and Natural Resources, with an amendment in the nature of a substitute, without written report
posts.summary: The bill would reauthorize the federal Snow Water Supply Forecasting Program, which helps predict water availability from snowpack for planning and water management purposes. It aims to continue funding and support for this program that assists water managers, farmers, and communities in the western United States prepare for seasonal water supplies.

posts.title: Ratepayer Protection Act
posts.label: ✅🏛️ Passed House with amendment (417-3)
posts.summary: The bill would require state utility regulators to consider adopting a standard that makes large data centers and similar high-demand facilities pay the full cost of any power plant, transmission line, or distribution upgrades needed to serve them, including costs if the customer later leaves. These "large-load customers" would need to provide financial guarantees or upfront payments to cover upgrade expenses before utilities proceed with any infrastructure work.
posts.meta: Energy and Commerce Committee · Rep. Gabe Evans (R-CO)
posts.whatsNext: To the Senate (if and when it takes it up)

posts.title: To require the Commissioner of U.S. Customs and Border Protection to link together applications of family members throughout the NEXUS application process, and for other purposes.
posts.label: ✅🏛️ Passed House (voice vote)
posts.summary: The bill would require U.S. Customs and Border Protection to allow family members applying for NEXUS—an expedited border inspection program between the United States and Canada—to link their applications together. It would let one family member schedule interviews for all linked relatives and give them the option to participate in joint interviews, while potentially allowing children under 14 to skip the interview requirement if linked to an eligible family member.
posts.meta: Homeland Security and Governmental Affairs Committee, Homeland Security Committee · Rep. Timothy Kennedy (D-NY)
posts.whatsNext: To the Senate (if and when it takes it up)

posts.title: Civil Preparedness for Agroterrorism Exercise Act of 2026
posts.label: ✅🏛️ Passed House (voice vote)
posts.summary: The bill would require the Department of Homeland Security to conduct a practice exercise within four years to test how federal, state, and local agencies and private companies could work together to prevent, respond to, and recover from a terrorist attack on U.S. agriculture and food systems, using a scenario involving the release of a biological agent. Within six months of completing the exercise, the department would need to report its findings and recommendations to Congress.
posts.meta: Homeland Security and Governmental Affairs Committee, Homeland Security Committee · Rep. Dale Strong (R-AL)
posts.whatsNext: To the Senate (if and when it takes it up)

posts.title: Water Resources Development Act of 2026
posts.label: ✅🏛️ Passed House with amendment (415-9)
posts.summary: The bill would authorize and modify various water infrastructure projects managed by the U.S. Army Corps of Engineers, including efforts to maintain ports and harbors, improve waterway navigation, reduce flood damage, restore ecosystems, protect shorelines, address harmful algal blooms, rehabilitate dams, and support water supply projects. It would also direct the Corps to establish a new office focused on speeding up project delivery and to create streamlined environmental approval processes for smaller harbor and river improvement projects.
posts.meta: Transportation and Infrastructure Committee · Rep. Sam Graves (R-MO)
posts.whatsNext: To the Senate (if and when it takes it up)

posts.label: ✅🏛️ Passed House (voice vote)
posts.summary: The bill would rename the U.S. Postal Service facility at 117 West Lovett Street in Charlotte, Michigan, as the "Francis C. Flaherty Post Office Building."
posts.meta: Oversight and Government Reform Committee · Rep. Tom Barrett (R-MI)

posts.title: National Fraud Enforcement Division Act of 2026
posts.label: ✅🏛️ Passed House (352-72)
posts.summary: The bill would formally establish a National Fraud Enforcement Division within the Department of Justice to investigate and prosecute fraud involving taxpayer dollars and federally funded programs.
posts.meta: Judiciary Committee · Rep. Brad Finstad (R-MN)
posts.whatsNext: To the Senate (if and when it takes it up)

posts.title: Fit Future Act
posts.label: ✅🏛️ Passed House with amendment (voice vote)
posts.summary: The bill would establish statutory authority for the President's Council on Sports, Fitness, and Nutrition, a federal advisory committee that provides recommendations on school-based physical education and nutrition. It would require the council to recommend youth fitness goals, strategies for promoting school physical education programs, campaigns to elevate U.S. sports and health, and approaches for reestablishing the Presidential Fitness Test with age- and gender-based exercise benchmarks. The bill would direct the Department of Health and Human Services to provide funding and support to the council, which could also receive funds from the National Fitness Foundation.
posts.meta: Health, Education, Labor, and Pensions Committee, Education and Workforce Committee · Rep. Ryan Mackenzie (R-PA)
posts.whatsNext: To the Senate (if and when it takes it up)

posts.title: Retire through Ownership Act
posts.label: ✅🏛️ Passed House (401-14)
posts.summary: The bill would clarify how Employee Stock Ownership Plans (ESOPs) determine the fair market value of company stock that isn't publicly traded, by allowing plan fiduciaries to rely on valuations from independent experts who follow established appraisal methodologies. This aims to give workers and plan managers greater confidence in the value assigned to their retirement benefits in closely held companies.
posts.meta: Health, Education, Labor, and Pensions Committee · Sen. Roger Marshall (R-KS)
posts.whatsNext: Presidential review (±10 days)

posts.title: Billion Dollar Boondoggle Act of 2025
posts.label: ✅🏛️ Passed House (voice vote)
posts.summary: The bill would require federal agencies to annually report to Congress on taxpayer-funded projects that are significantly over budget or behind schedule—specifically those delayed more than five years or costing at least $1 billion more than originally estimated. These reports would include details about why projects fell behind, how their scope changed, current completion dates and costs, and any bonuses paid to contractors, with the information compiled and published online by the Office of Management and Budget.
posts.meta: Small Business and Entrepreneurship Committee, Homeland Security and Governmental Affairs Committee · Sen. Joni Ernst (R-IA)

posts.title: Equal Campus Access Act of 2026
posts.label: 📋 Reported by committee
posts.note: Education and Workforce, as amended, H. Rept. 119-833
posts.summary: The bill would prohibit federal funding under the Higher Education Act from going to public colleges and universities that treat religious student groups differently than other student organizations. It aims to ensure that religious groups receive the same campus rights, benefits, and privileges as non-religious student organizations, regardless of their beliefs, practices, or membership standards.
posts.meta: Education and Workforce Committee · Rep. Tim Walberg (R-MI)
posts.whatsNext: Floor scheduling (leadership decides if and when it gets a vote)

posts.title: Cold Weather Diesel Reliability Act of 2025
posts.label: 📋 Reported by committee
posts.note: Environment and Public Works, with an amendment in the nature of a substitute, without written report
posts.summary: The bill would require the EPA to allow manufacturers of certain vehicles to temporarily disable engine shutdown or power-reduction features during extended cold weather periods. This aims to improve diesel vehicle reliability and performance in harsh winter conditions while those protective functions are suspended.
posts.meta: Environment and Public Works Committee · Sen. Dan Sullivan (R-AK)
posts.whatsNext: Floor scheduling (leadership decides if and when it gets a vote)

posts.title: Protect College Sports Act of 2026
posts.label: 🗳️ Motion to proceed filed
posts.summary: The bill would protect college athletes' rights to earn money from their names, images, and likenesses by prohibiting schools from restricting these deals, while requiring athletes to disclose compensation above $600 and capping agent fees at 5%. It would also grant athletes one penalty-free transfer, restrict coaches from switching teams mid-season, establish limits on how schools can compensate athletes to avoid circumventing revenue-sharing rules, and allow schools and conferences to jointly sell sports broadcasting rights under limited antitrust protections.
posts.meta: Commerce, Science, and Transportation Committee · Sen. Ted Cruz (R-TX)

posts.title: Wildfire Emissions Prevention Act of 2026
posts.label: 📋 Reported by committee
posts.note: Environment and Public Works, without amendment, without written report
posts.summary: The bill would amend federal clean air regulations to change how air quality is monitored and reported during prescribed fires—controlled burns used to reduce wildfire risk. It aims to prevent emissions from these preventive fire management practices from being counted against air quality standards in the same way as other pollution sources.
posts.meta: Environment and Public Works Committee · Sen. John Curtis (R-UT)

posts.title: Prison Staff Safety Enhancement Act

posts.summary: The law establishes national standards for the Bureau of Prisons to prevent, reduce, and punish sexual harassment and sexual assault committed by incarcerated individuals against prison staff. It also requires the Bureau of Prisons to implement recommendations from a Department of Justice Inspector General report on addressing these incidents.
posts.meta: Judiciary Committee · Sen. Marsha Blackburn (R-TN)
posts.whatsNext: Takes effect (on enactment unless the text sets other dates)

posts.summary: The law designates College Station as an additional location where court proceedings must be held in the Galveston Division of the Southern District of Texas, and similarly establishes El Centro as a required court location in the Southern District of California.
posts.meta: Judiciary Committee · Sen. Ted Cruz (R-TX)
posts.whatsNext: Takes effect (on enactment unless the text sets other dates)

posts.title: Department of Homeland Security Intelligence and Analysis Training Act
posts.label: ✅🏛️ Passed House with amendment (voice vote)
posts.summary: The bill would require the Department of Homeland Security's Office of Intelligence and Analysis to establish standardized training programs for new employees covering privacy rights, civil liberties, and intelligence standards, with specialized curricula tailored to different job roles such as analysts and open-source intelligence collectors. It would also require the office to track training completion and direct the Government Accountability Office to report to Congress on how these new training programs compare to those offered by other intelligence agencies.
posts.meta: Homeland Security and Governmental Affairs Committee, Homeland Security Committee · Rep. Seth Magaziner (D-RI)
posts.whatsNext: To the Senate (if and when it takes it up)

posts.title: I&A Mission Reorientation Act of 2026
posts.label: ✅🏛️ Passed House with amendment (voice vote)
posts.summary: The bill would require the Department of Homeland Security's intelligence office to treat state, local, tribal, territorial, and private sector partners as equally important to other parts of the federal intelligence community in receiving intelligence support. It would direct the office to improve two-way information sharing with these partners, deploy intelligence capabilities to help identify threats, maintain strong relationships with regional fusion centers, and ensure that serving these partners is not sidelined by other duties—then report to Congress on progress in making these changes.
posts.meta: Homeland Security and Governmental Affairs Committee, Homeland Security Committee · Rep. August Pfluger (R-TX)
posts.whatsNext: To the Senate (if and when it takes it up)

posts.title: Bankruptcy Threshold Adjustment Act
posts.label: ✅🏛️ Passed House with amendment (voice vote)
posts.summary: The bill would increase the debt limits for small business reorganization bankruptcies and wage earner bankruptcies that had previously expired. Specifically, it aims to raise the threshold for small business reorganizations from approximately $3.4 million to $7.5 million, increase the wage earner bankruptcy limit from approximately $2.1 million to $2.75 million, and change how debt is counted under wage earner bankruptcies to include both secured and unsecured debt toward a single limit.
posts.meta: Judiciary Committee · Rep. Ben Cline (R-VA)
posts.whatsNext: To the Senate (if and when it takes it up)

posts.title: Safe Cloud Storage Act
posts.label: ✅🏛️ Passed House with amendment (voice vote)
posts.summary: The bill would extend legal protections to cloud storage companies that work with law enforcement agencies to store evidence of child sexual abuse material during investigations. It would shield these vendors from civil lawsuits and criminal charges as long as they follow cybersecurity standards and don't act with intentional misconduct, negligence, malice, or reckless disregard.
posts.meta: Judiciary Committee · Rep. Laurel Lee (R-FL)
posts.whatsNext: To the Senate (if and when it takes it up)

posts.title: Science of Reading Act of 2026
posts.label: ✅🏛️ Passed House with amendment (voice vote)
posts.summary: The bill would modify a federal grant program for literacy instruction to require that funded programs align with "science of reading" principles—emphasizing phonics, phonemic awareness, vocabulary, fluency, and comprehension—while explicitly excluding instructional methods that rely primarily on context clues or visual memory for word recognition. It aims to direct federal education funding toward evidence-based reading instruction approaches supported by research.
posts.meta: Education and Workforce Committee · Rep. Erin Houchin (R-IN)
posts.whatsNext: To the Senate (if and when it takes it up)

posts.title: To designate the facility of the United States Postal Service located at 189 East Main Street in Xenia, Ohio, as the "Gilman 'Gil' Whitney Post Office Building".

posts.summary: The bill would rename the U.S. Postal Service facility at 189 East Main Street in Xenia, Ohio, to honor it as the "Gilman 'Gil' Whitney Post Office Building."

posts.summary: The bill would expand existing restrictions on who can hold union leadership positions by adding individuals convicted of sex offenses against minors to the list of people barred from serving in such roles for 13 years after their conviction or release from prison. Currently, similar bans apply only to those convicted of crimes like robbery, bribery, burglary, murder, or rape.

posts.whatsNext: To the Senate (if and when it takes it up)

posts.title: Foreign Service Modernization Act
posts.label: ✅🏛️ Passed House with amendment (voice vote)
posts.summary: The bill would modernize the Foreign Service by requiring the State Department to develop plans for diplomats to work in high-risk environments, establish programs to recruit military veterans, and create a reserve corps for emergency staffing needs. It would also mandate leadership training for officers before promotions, protect the careers of those pursuing external education, and require foreign language-trained diplomats to serve in positions using those languages.
posts.meta: Ways and Means Committee, Foreign Affairs Committee · Rep. Michael Lawler (R-NY)
posts.whatsNext: To the Senate (if and when it takes it up)

posts.title: National Fossil Act of 2026

posts.whatsNext: To the Senate (if and when it takes it up)

posts.title: PEARL Act
posts.label: ✅🏛️ Passed House with amendment (voice vote)
posts.summary: The bill would require U.S. Customs and Border Protection to create a pilot program that adopts dogs from local animal shelters and trains them to serve as support animals for CBP personnel, helping with grief, trauma, and morale.
posts.meta: Homeland Security Committee · Rep. David Joyce (R-OH)
posts.whatsNext: To the Senate (if and when it takes it up)

posts.title: Transportation Worker Identification Credential Efficiency Act
posts.label: ✅🏛️ Passed House with amendment (voice vote)
posts.summary: The bill would require the Transportation Security Administration to develop guidelines helping incarcerated people prepare applications for a Transportation Worker Identification Credential before their release from prison, as well as guidelines for appealing denials of the credential. The credential is required for workers needing access to secure areas at U.S. maritime facilities and vessels.
posts.meta: Commerce, Science, and Transportation Committee, Homeland Security Committee · Rep. Troy Carter (D-LA)
posts.whatsNext: To the Senate (if and when it takes it up)

posts.title: Lindsey O. Graham Sanctioning Russia and Iran Act of 2026
posts.label: ✅🏛️ Agreed to other chamber's amendments (262-159)
posts.summary: The bill would impose various sanctions against Russia, including visa and property-blocking sanctions on Russian leaders and military officials, tariffs of up to 100% on goods from countries that continue buying Russian oil and gas, and prohibitions on U.S. exports of energy to Russia and American investments in Russian entities. It would also extend Iran sanctions laws through 2031 and expand a federal tax deduction for educator expenses to include early childhood educators.
posts.meta: Ways and Means Committee · Rep. Jimmy Panetta (D-CA)
posts.whatsNext: Presidential review (±10 days)

posts.title: Northern Border Security Enhancement and Review Act
posts.label: ✅🏛️ Passed House with amendment (voice vote)
posts.summary: The bill would require the Department of Homeland Security to conduct a threat analysis of the northern U.S. border every two years, examining terrorist and criminal threats and evaluating whether additional screening measures at border crossings could prevent dangerous individuals from entering the country. It would also require the department to update its northern border security strategy based on each analysis and brief Congress on findings, while tasking the agency's Air and Marine Operations unit with developing performance measures to assess how effectively it secures the northern border in air and maritime areas.
posts.meta: Homeland Security Committee · Rep. Nicholas Langworthy (R-NY)

posts.title: PROOF Act
posts.label: ✅🏛️ Passed House (217-207)
posts.summary: The bill would require states to share information with federal law enforcement agencies to help investigate and prosecute fraud in major federal assistance programs, including Medicaid, food stamps, and temporary aid to families. It aims to protect privacy by limiting how federal agencies can use the shared information—only for fraud-related investigations—and requires the Department of Justice to report annually to Congress on how often it requests this information and what results those investigations produce.

posts.title: Protect College Sports Act of 2026
posts.label: ⏱️ Cloture invoked (on taking up the bill) (74-24)

posts.summary: The bill would authorize the Department of the Army to transfer a 20-acre parcel of land at Fort Bragg to North Carolina at no cost. The state would use the property to build a veterans' home to care for disabled veterans and provide nursing care, with North Carolina covering all costs associated with the transfer. The land would revert to federal ownership if it stops being used for the veterans' home.
posts.meta: Armed Services Committee · Rep. Richard Hudson (R-NC)

posts.title: Common Cents Act
posts.label: ✅🏛️ Passed House (voice vote)
posts.summary: The bill would stop the U.S. Treasury from minting pennies for general circulation (though pennies would remain legal tender) and require cash transactions to be rounded to the nearest nickel. It would also allow the Treasury to change the material composition of nickels and establish procedures for discontinuing other coins if Congress is notified.

posts.title: Legislative Branch Agencies Clarification Act
posts.label: ✅🏛️ Passed House (voice vote)
posts.summary: The bill would change how three top legislative branch officials are appointed and removed. It would shift the appointment of the Librarian of Congress and the Director of the Government Publishing Office from the President to a bipartisan congressional commission, and allow their removal only through a vote by congressional leaders. The bill would also make the Register of Copyrights a presidentially appointed position (rather than appointed by the Librarian), remove the Library of Congress's authority over the Copyright Office, create an inspector general office within the Copyright Office, and require the Government Publishing Office to establish a human resources management system.
posts.meta: Oversight and Government Reform Committee, Judiciary Committee, House Administration · Rep. H. Griffith (R-VA)

posts.summary: The bill would transfer federal lands in northern Nevada to state and local governments, as well as the Washoe Tribe, for economic development and public purposes. It would also designate certain parcels as protected wilderness areas, allow the state to repurpose a former prison site, enable the federal government to establish a regional office complex in Nevada, and protect tribal lands.

It would also require NOAA to report names of personnel involved in harassment or assault claims to the Coast Guard, prohibit people convicted of certain sexual offenses from working at NOAA, and expand reporting requirements on these incidents.
